subject: Missing online racing
author: Xandu
body:
I'm missing online racing with bikes and leaderboards for timed bike challenges. I hope this is something that is already in the pack but just locked for some reason.

Appart from that I enjoy the bike pack and the day/night cycle makes the city come more alive although the colors get very gray and dull at times.

-- The Creator --

subject: Night time...
author: Gooner Rhyle
body: ...is a bit bland. Think they just made it dark instead of turning Paradise City into a Neon playground...hardly seems like it's brimming with life does it?

subject: Harder in the turns
author: Aaboe
body:
I like the bikes a lot, but they're quite a lot harder to turn than a car... and I'm missing the handbrake 😉

But it's fun driving them and I've *never* done time rules so fast before. Easy to weave around. Night time is creepy IMO, since it's harder to see where you are and where you're going. Already now I've had some unexpected *things* point out that I crashed into. I didn't even know what it was!

I'm glad I got it and despite some opinions that it doesn't really fit, I at least think it's all in good fun. Now I "just" need that bigger television so I can actually read what it says when I've completed a challenge thingie... 😉

Laters...

Aaboe  [gamercard:aaboe]

subject: Burnout Bike Controls
author: yolkum
body:
The motorcycles and environmental add-ons are great additions to Paradise. 
Criterion definitely has created the best gaming community experience around and to offer up what is essential a new game for free in an industry where companies are charging for every little gimmick add-on they can think of is truly awesome.
 
I just had a few questions...
Why do the bikes only have one brake control? I've been a biker for over 10 years now and I was surprised when I started playing that I couldn't use the individual brakes to effect how the bike controls? The current braking system acts very much as it would if you applied both brakes at the same time evenly, which is fine in safe day to day riding. Then again this is Burnout and there is nothing safe about that.
 
I was hoping that on a curve or ramp you would be able to slam your rear brake and lock it up making your bikes rear end whip out and throw it into a spin. This would be great off of ramps  and other jumps. Much like the e-brake works on the cars.  The loss of spins was kind of a shock, it's such a major part of what makes the cars fun.  Also since they went with crotch rocket bikes, if you had the ability to control only the front break it would be great for bringing the bike up on it's front tire and gliding on it. I mean this wouldn't work on a Harley with a raked out front end, but would be perfect for the current bikes.  This could blow stunt runs wide open for motorcycles. 
Don't get me wrong, I'm loving this and am extremely happy. I just see so much potential for the bikes in paradise.  
 
Here's a great video of individual braking. http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eLvLjajdw80
 
 
Josh
